originalTitle: Is 'Trumpflation' real? Why Wall Street fears this could be a reason for stock market crash
simplifiedContent: There's a worry on Wall Street that something called "Trumpflation" might cause the stock market to crash. This concern is growing because of rising prices and higher interest rates. The main issue is that core inflation, which measures how fast prices are rising, is at 3.3% and doesn't seem to be going down, which could lead the Federal Reserve to keep interest rates high or even raise them. This matters because higher interest rates can make it harder for companies to grow and make money, which can then affect the stock market. As a result, some people are worried that the high values of stocks might not be sustainable.

originalTitle: World Bank's IFC, HDFC AMC invest in Molbio Diagnostics' Rs 281 crore IPO anchor round
simplifiedContent: Molbio Diagnostics, a company based in Goa, is planning to raise money by selling its shares to the public, known as an Initial Public Offering (IPO). Before the IPO opens on August 10, the company has already raised Rs 281 crore from a few big investors, including the World Bank's IFC and HDFC Mutual Fund. This is called an "anchor round" and it's a good sign for the company. The company also got Rs 160 crore from some of its existing investors selling their shares. Some big brokerages think the IPO is a good investment, which is why they're recommending that people "subscribe" to it, or buy the shares.

originalTitle: Market Trading Guide: Jindal Saw among 2 stock recommendations for Monday
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the stock market news: Some companies in India have recently released their financial results, and most of them have done as well as or even better than expected. This is making investors feel more positive about certain sectors of the economy. As a result, the market is suggesting that investors consider buying stocks like Jindal Saw on Monday. This could be a good opportunity for investors to make some money. The overall mood in the market is optimistic, which is why these stock recommendations are being made.

originalTitle: US Markets Week Ahead: Inflation, retail sales, home sales and earnings in focus
simplifiedContent: This week, investors will be paying close attention to several important reports about the US economy. These reports will show how much prices are rising (inflation), how well retailers are selling their products (retail sales), and how the housing market is doing (home sales). They will also be looking at how people are feeling about the economy (consumer sentiment survey) and listening to companies' financial results (earnings). This information is important because it will help investors understand how strong the US economy is and what the Federal Reserve might do next with interest rates. By watching these reports, investors hope to get a better sense of what's happening in the economy and make informed decisions about their investments.

originalTitle: The stock market is finally rising again—and it’s getting cheaper, too
simplifiedContent: The stock market, which is like a big place where people buy and sell pieces of companies, has been going up lately. In the past year, one important group of companies, called the S&P 500, has increased in value by 22%. Even though the market is going up, the prices of these companies are actually becoming more reasonable, or "cheaper", compared to their value. This is a good thing because it means that investors can buy into the market at a more affordable price. The combination of a rising market and more reasonable prices is a positive sign for people who want to invest in the stock market.

originalTitle: Upcoming IPOs: Shiprocket IPO, Dhoot Transmission IPO among new issues to open next week; full list here
simplifiedContent: Next week, some new companies will be selling shares to the public for the first time, including Shiprocket and Dhoot Transmission. This is called an Initial Public Offering (IPO). These IPOs will be open for people to buy shares from August 10 to 12. At the same time, shares from eight other companies that started selling last week will start trading on the market. This means that people who bought those shares will be able to sell them or buy more, and see how their investments are doing.
